dimensions.reasons: The authored animation frames, especially Group C frame_0001, reproduce the reference's core aquarium tableau: orange-and-white fish at left and lower center, a large orange fish on the right, a partly cropped bronze fish at lower right, driftwood at left, dark rocks and pale gravel below, plants at right, bubbles, and a blue-lit background. The reference framing and strong blue underwater mood are clearly recognizable.
issues: The fish are much more stylized and cleanly CG-rendered than the softer, more natural-looking reference fish.
The rear wall is a distinct tiled/relief panel and the blue ridged mound at right is more conspicuous than the softer background forms in the reference.

Later Group C frames, notably frame_0011 through frame_0016, feature the largest fish turning nearly vertical and visually dominating/crowding the right side, which departs from the predominantly horizontal passes visible in the supplied reference frames.

dimensions.reasons: Driftwood, rocks, gravel, and plant stems visibly connect to the sand in the main views, and swimming fish do not require floor support. However, Group A detail_three_quarter and wide_three_quarter expose the scene as an open set: the sand is a thin rectangular slab and the rear wall ends at open dark space without a coherent tank enclosure.
issues: The exposed side/outer edges of the rear wall and thin sand plane terminate into empty space in Group A oblique views.
No visible side, ceiling, front glass, or complete room/tank shell is present in the evaluator multi-view geometry.

Several animated fish and rigid fins overlap closely or ambiguously pass through neighboring fish and the plant cluster, such as the vertically oriented large fish in Group A wide_motion_end and Group C frame_0014.

dimensions.reasons: The fish independently read as goldfish rather than generic blobs: Group C frame_0001 clearly shows orange/pale bellies, forked tails, dorsal fins, eyes, and visible scale relief. The orange, white, bronze, green, dark-rock, pale-substrate, and saturated blue palette aligns well with the reference.
issues: The eyes are disproportionately large, glossy, and cartoon-like relative to the reference.
Fins read as very thin rigid triangular sheets with conspicuous parallel line patterning rather than soft organic translucent fins.
Fish colors and scale relief are cleaner and more pastel/plastic-looking than the reference's softer, murkier underwater coloration.

dimensions.reasons: The authored final frames have a coherent underwater image with convincing blue illumination, particulate specks, bubble streams, depth layering, fish motion blur, textured rocks, and visible scale detail. Group C frame_0008 is a particularly readable, polished aquarium shot.
issues: The overall result reads as a stylized CG diorama rather than a natural aquarium video because of oversized eyes, planar fins, and uniform fish modeling.
The fish bodies, gravel distribution, and textured rear panel are overly regular and clean.
Motion blur on some fins and rapidly turning fish makes silhouettes and depth separation unclear, for example around the central cluster in Group C frame_0014 and frame_0015.

dimensions.reasons: The final animation maintains the key reference relationships: left-side driftwood behind a left fish, a right-side plant cluster behind/right of the main fish, rocks and gravel along the bottom, a front-facing red-and-white fish near center, and a lower-right bronze fish. Group C frame_0001 closely follows the reference's foreground/background staging.
issues: The right side becomes substantially more crowded than the reference as the largest fish turns nose-down among plant stems.
The large blue ridged mound behind the plant has a stronger, more geometric presence than the relatively subdued right-background decoration in the reference.
Some fish passes place tails and fins directly across other fish without a clear depth gap, reducing readability of the intended foreground/background staging.

dimensions.reasons: Fish size hierarchy is sensible and broadly reference-like: the upper/right orange fish is largest, the left and lower-middle fish are medium, and the bronze lower-right fish is partly cropped. Driftwood, plant height, rock clusters, and substrate also have generally convincing relative scale in Group C frame_0001 and Group A hero_start.
issues: The largest fish becomes disproportionately dominant during its vertical turn in later animation frames.
Several fish share nearly identical body/fins proportions despite the reference presenting more varied natural goldfish silhouettes.
The very broad exposed sand sheet in Group A three-quarter views makes the aquarium dressing read smaller and more stage-like than in the final framing.

dimensions.reasons: Blue overhead/side illumination, bright water glow, scale highlights, dark matte rocks, pale gravel, bubbles, and translucent fish fins establish the intended underwater material and lighting language. Group C frame_0001 and Group A hero_mid show strong blue light and readable orange fish contrast comparable to the reference.
issues: The water is clearer and more uniformly studio-lit than the reference's softer, hazier aquarium-video appearance.
Fish skin and scales look somewhat plasticky and evenly embossed rather than naturally irregular.
Fin line patterns and sharp translucent planes remain visually prominent instead of blending into soft fin material.

dimensions.reasons: All important scene categories are present in the renders: multiple poseable-looking goldfish of several color patterns, driftwood, dark rock clusters, pale sandy/gravel substrate, right-side stem plants, blue rear environment, suspended particles, and rising bubbles. The rendered fish count also covers the prominent and partial fish roles seen in the reference.
issues: The submission adds a conspicuous ridged blue mound/background object that is not clearly matched to a specific reference element.
The surrounding aquarium structure itself is incomplete when inspected off the authored camera, with no coherent visible enclosure in Group A oblique views.

criteria.criterion: The aquarium contains multiple recognizable orange goldfish with reference-like principal anatomy.
criteria.evidence: The animation frames clearly show a group of orange, pale-orange, and red-white goldfish with readable oval bodies, heads, large eyes, dorsal/pectoral fins, and forked tails.

criteria.criterion: The fish group shows reference-like variation in relative size, body proportions, and tail form.
criteria.evidence: The group includes a notably large elongated upper-right fish, a smaller round red-and-white fish near center, medium orange-white swimmers, and a bronze lower fish; their tail sizes and fork proportions visibly vary.

criteria.criterion: Visible underwater bubbles are integrated into the aquarium.
criteria.evidence: Small bright bubble streams are visible rising above and beside the right-side plant cluster throughout the animation frames.

criteria.criterion: The tank contains the reference-defining plants, branching driftwood, dark rocks, and pale substrate.
criteria.evidence: The scene visibly contains leafy green stem plants at right, a large branching driftwood form at left, clustered dark rocks, scattered pebbles, and a pale sandy floor.

criteria.criterion: The principal environmental components follow the reference arrangement.
criteria.evidence: A thick forked branch rises diagonally through the left/center background, while tall plants occupy the right and the rock-and-sand treatment remains beneath the fish.

criteria.criterion: Fish occupy distinct depth planes and create readable foreground/background layering.
criteria.evidence: The large orange fish dominates the upper-right foreground, smaller fish occupy the center and left, and partial fish at the lower and upper edges establish additional depth layers and changing overlaps.

criteria.criterion: The fish group has the close reference view's prominent central scale, occupancy, and overlap density.
criteria.evidence: The delivered animation uses a close view with several large swimmers filling the middle and right of frame, including overlapping central red-white/orange fish and edge-cropped fish.

criteria.criterion: The fish reproduce the reference's varied orange and gold coloration, lighter markings, wet bodies, and softer translucent fins.
criteria.evidence: Fish have differentiated salmon-orange, muted bronze, orange-white, and red-white markings; visible scale relief catches wet highlights and the fins/tails are thin, ribbed, and partly translucent.

criteria.criterion: Plant, driftwood, rock, and substrate materials retain the reference's distinct color and surface character.
criteria.evidence: The plant stems read clearly as green leafy vegetation, the branch and rock clusters are dark blue-gray with visible surface texture, and the bottom is a light sand layer scattered with pale gravel.

criteria.criterion: The scene has a strong reference-like underwater blue lighting and atmospheric treatment.
criteria.evidence: Strong cyan-blue light dominates the fish, rock-wall background, branch, and substrate, with cool highlights, blue haze, and a bright overhead glow.

criteria.criterion: Every visible fish remains practically poseable through a usable editable setup in the Blender project.
Fish swimming is visibly propelled by repeated lateral tail strokes.
criteria.evidence: Across the sampled sequence, fish bodies translate and turn, but their forked tails mostly retain similar sheet-like poses or are motion-blurred; repeated alternating lateral tail deflections are not unambiguously readable.

criteria.criterion: Multiple fish perform passes that change their relative positions and overlaps.
criteria.evidence: Relative positions change substantially: the large upper-right fish transitions into a near-vertical pass, the red-white fish moves through the central/lower group, and fish occlusions change by the final frames.

criteria.criterion: The broad ordering and pace of major fish turns, passes, and foreground crossings follow the reference.
criteria.evidence: The sequence begins with a dense central cluster, then develops into pronounced crossings: the large fish turns nose-down near the right side while the red-white swimmer advances across the lower foreground late in the clip.

criteria.criterion: The composition reproduces the reference's close aquarium view and readable principal anchors.
criteria.evidence: The exported animation is a close, mostly straight-on aquarium shot with a readable fish cluster framed by the left driftwood mass and tall right-side plants.

criteria.criterion: Camera behavior matches the reference's restrained continuous close view.
criteria.evidence: The textured rear wall, driftwood, plant stems, and floor retain effectively stable framing across the ordered video frames; the apparent action comes from fish movement rather than a dramatic camera move or cut.

criteria.criterion: The submitted content render has the requested format, encoding, dimensions, frame rate, and source-like duration.
The delivered .blend is an editable source project containing the recreated scene and animation.

notes: This is a strong recognizable aquarium reconstruction with closely matched subject inventory, blue staging, fish hierarchy, and an actual animated sequence. Its main limitations are the more cartoon-like fish design, rigid planar fins and occasional crowded/intersecting passes, plus an open thin-set tank construction exposed by evaluator multi-views.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
